title: The Forbidden Win
reviewNotes: Reconstructed the rook/knight staircase from the initial six-piece position; checked actual knight mate, immediate stalemate and a drawing pawn capture. Corrected the source’s uniqueness claim: Rh1 is not the only win.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only a true genius would be able to find the incredible win that black has in this position. At first glance, it seems like black is completely winning, but then we realize that white is only two steps away from getting a new queen. And if we try to block the escape of the king, actually this is going to be a stalemate. White is not in check, but it doesn't have any legal moves, so this would be a draw. And if instead of this, black starts capturing the pawns, this actually doesn't stop the king from going to G7, attacking the rook, and after the rook moves, white is going to promote. Black will have to give up the rook for the queen, and this would still be a draw by insufficient material. So, what is black to do in this position? Well, there is a surprising idea here that starts with the majestic rook to H1, stepping away as far as possible from the action, and yet this is the only winning move. White's only legal moves are either king to G7 or to G8, but once the king comes out, now black can give a check on G1 and force the king back to H8. But what progress have we made? This is still a stalemate, unless we move the rook, right? Well, not exactly. There is another way to prevent the stalemate, and that move is knight to G2. We use our own knight to cover the view of the rook and prevent the stalemate. And after the king comes back outside, now after we move the knight, we are going to give another check with the rook. So, what this means is that this position is a knight staircase. We're going to give a discovered check with the rook, force the king in the corner, and then cover the view of the rook again with the knight. And this little maneuver has allowed us to bring the knight into the game. And after the king comes out, a simple maneuver is going to prepare knight to F7, checkmate.
